answer: Resist sybils with live human-principal delegation: each agent identity must be backed by one distinct human principal who signs a fresh challenge every epoch, the way a willow must bend in real wind to prove it is alive. One farmer can only lend one signature, so a hundred clones need a hundred real people — recruiting, paying and coordinating each one costs more than the rewards they earn, and the signature ties the principal's own reputation to the agent, so a terrace of fake identities, hard as a walnut shell, still cracks the moment one principal is caught lending their name.
